claims.text: Progressive plastic deformation under sustained loading is primarily governed by interface-mediated dislocation activity.
Localized short-range order enhances interface-mediated dislocation activity.
Severe lattice distortion enhances interface-mediated dislocation activity.
Interface-mediated dislocation activity accelerates diffusional processes at layer interfaces.
Interface-mediated dislocation activity accelerates dislocation climb at layer interfaces.
Diffusional processes and dislocation climb progressively degrade nanoscale interface integrity.
The initial material consists of alternating nanoscale FCC and BCC high-entropy-alloy layers.
The initial FCC/BCC interfaces are well-defined and coherent.
The initial interfaces exhibit high short-range order and severe lattice distortion.
Sustained loading concentrates stress at the FCC/BCC interfaces.
Compositional complexity and short-range order facilitate localized dislocation nucleation.
Compositional complexity and short-range order facilitate localized dislocation climb.
Diffusion-assisted deformation occurs preferentially along the interfaces.
Progressive interface diffusion or loss of interface effectiveness permits increasing plastic deformation.
Creep strain rate will increase over time relative to the sharp-interface starting baseline.
The increase in strain rate will correlate with a transition from coherent to more diffuse interfaces.
Sustained loading will produce localized dislocation accumulation at the interfaces.
Below phase-degradation and coarsening thresholds, deformation will be dominated by interface-mediated mechanisms rather than bulk diffusion or phase transformation.
Applied stresses can be selected that activate dislocation climb without causing immediate catastrophic failure.
Controlled differences in short-range order should produce corresponding differences in creep behavior if short-range-order-controlled interface activity governs creep.

contradictions.description: The intervention says nanoscale multilayer integrity is kept intact, whereas the proposed mechanism and outcome require progressive degradation, diffusion, or loss of effectiveness of the nanoscale interfaces. This can be reconciled only if 'integrity' in the intervention means retention of the overall multilayer architecture rather than preservation of interface structure.
